today.tagline: Create and edit videos by chatting
today.description: Make videos with Claude, ChatGPT, or any AI agent. Give Clueso an idea, deck, reference video, or recording, and it handles the whole video production: storyboard, scenes, voiceover, music, and editing, on-brand. Everything stays editable, by hand or by chat.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt Community! 👋I’m Neel, co-founder of Clueso.We launched Clueso here last year with a pretty simple idea: turn rough screen recordings into polished product videos in minutes.The response was incredible. Thousands of people started using Clueso, and this community made us #1 Product of the Day, Week, and Month.Over the last year, we kept seeing people push Clueso beyond what we originally built it for. They wanted to start with more than a screen recording. They wanted to make more kinds of videos. And increasingly, they wanted AI to do more of the actual work.So today we’re launching Clueso MCP.Now you can create and edit videos directly from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible agent.Give it a prompt and whatever material you have: a screen recording, deck, document, URL, Figma file, raw footage, reference video you like, or just an idea.Clueso takes it from there. It plans the video, creates the scenes, writes the script, generates the AI voiceover, adds music, motion graphics, captions and animations, edits everything together, and applies your branding.In fact, our product hunt launch video above was made entirely with Clueso MCP.Basically, you tell it what you want to make, and it makes the video with you.The part we care a lot about is control.A lot of AI video tools feel like black boxes: you prompt them, get a finished clip back, and if something isn’t quite right, your main option is to keep regenerating.Clueso is different because there’s a powerful video editor underneath the agent. Everything it creates remains editable. You can open the project and change anything yourself, or just keep chatting with the agent.You could be a marketer making a launch video, a founder making a product demo, a freelancer creating something for a client, a small business making marketing content, or just someone with an idea they want to turn into a great video.Here’s what you can do with it:Create from inspiration. Give Clueso a few videos you like or a moodboard. It understands the look, feel, and creative direction you’re going for, then creates a full video around your own content, product, and brand.Create pretty much any kind of video. Launch and marketing videos, product demos, walkthroughs, tutorials, explainers, social content, complex motion graphics, animated sequences, logo animations and more.Edit however you want. Jump into the Clueso editor and make changes yourself, or just chat with the agent and ask it to make the edits for you.Build custom workflows around video. Because Clueso works through MCP, you can connect it with tools like Figma, Slack, Linear, social platforms, your CRM, support tools and more and make video creation, editing and distribution part of a larger automated workflow.So a feature can ship and turn into a launch video, a finished design can become an explainer, or a completed video can automatically move into the next step of your workflow.Making a video no longer has to start with opening a video editor. You can tell your agent what you need, let it do the work, and still have complete control whenever you want to jump in yourself.Special offer for the PH community:To celebrate our launch, we’re offering a 50% discount on all plans for the first month to first-time subscribers! Use the code PHXCLUESO50 at checkout. Offer valid until September 25, 11:59 pm PT.Want to try it? Connect the Clueso MCP from here: https://clueso.io/mcpThe support from this community last year was honestly overwhelming. You made us Product of the Month, and we’d love your support again today. ❤️I’ll be in the comments all day, so try it, show us what you make, and tell us what works, what doesn’t, and what you’d like to see next.Huge thanks to @KevinWilliamDavid for hunting us!

today.description: Your data changes constantly. Anomalo Analyst tells you what matters before you know to ask. comments.text: Hey Product Hunt, I'm Elliot, co-founder and CEO of Anomalo.I've spent years working with data — growth and product roles at @instacart and @LinkedIn, then building enterprise data quality tools at @Anomalo . I’ve seen that some of the biggest lessons often came from changes in the data. At Instacart, launching one new retailer surfaced an engagement spike that reshaped our growth strategy for years. At LinkedIn, small experiments in network-building tools moved user behavior enough to reset our roadmap.But spotting those data changes is hard. You need dashboards for everything that matters and someone watching obsessively. Even with teams of analysts, we missed a lot.That's why we built Analyst. Using technology Anomalo pioneered for data quality monitoring, it learns what's normal for your data, then uses AI to spot and explain meaningful changes — creating an automatic news feed of what moved and why.Most data tools only answer the questions you thought to ask. The valuable data changes are often the ones nobody asked about: a paid social campaign that spiked purchases but only for certain SKUs, a supplier whose delivery times crept up 52% over a quarter, a metric that degraded only because of a mix shift. Anomalo Analyst spots these changes for you. Just connect @DataBricks , BigQuery, or @Snowflake , read-only, and tell Analyst what matters in each table so the insights are tailored. You’ll start seeing Analyst insights in the first few days. Each insight includes a business summary, a technical summary, and the underlying logic and investigative steps. Free to start. today.name: SereneDB
today.tagline: Ultra-Fast Search & Analytics Database, Agentic AI ready
today.description: SereneDB is the result of 12 years of development - an open-source database that does ultra-fast full-text and fast analytics in one engine. Postgres- and Elastic-compatible: keep your SQL, your drivers, and your Elastic clients; drop the second system and the ETL between them. In our public benchmark, it outperforms Elasticsearch, ClickHouse, and Postgres search extensions, and indexes 1B logs in under 8 minutes at ~10x less disk. Apache 2.0, methodology, and raw results are public.
today.category: Open Source • Developer Tools • GitHub • Database

comments.text: SereneDB built something that is usually available only to big-wallet vendors: a database that holds a huge amount of data in one node, on an ordinary machine, and does ultra-fast search plus analytics at an enterprise level. Their full-text search is the fastest today, based on benchmarks anyone can verify.And all this -- open source!I have a Master's in CS, but it was a long time ago, and I completely forgot how to code. I still remember the fundamentals of how to build software, though. This era of vibecoding is my renaissance: I use AI to build what I have wanted to create for a long time. One component was missing -- an easy-to-use database. Yes, there is Postgres, but you need real skills to set it up and tune it. With SereneDB I just paste the line into Claude Code, connect the docs MCP, and work (I had to install Docker along the way, though). Now I have almost no limit on data volume: these are enterprise-level datasets I can search and analyze on ordinary virtual machines.Imagine how much freedom that gives to scientists all over the world: all of PubMed's 37 million abstracts, NOAA's daily climate records from 100,000+ stations, every photo NASA's Mars rovers have ever sent back -- searchable and analyzable on an ordinary VM, by one person with a coding assistant. And imagine how many more use cases they will come up with by pairing their AI coding assistants with SereneDB.I'm proud to be the team's hunter. They see the future, and they built the missing component for it: a vibecoder-friendly, top-level database.

comments.text: Hey PH, Johannes here. This started as an embarrassing internal failure. At Swat.io we run a social media management tool for 1,700+ brands, so we thought getting our own people posting on LinkedIn would be easy and obvious. Seven signed up. Two to three were still posting a month later. The rest? Did not know what to write about, did not stay motivated enough over time. Our very own social media manager tried to keep momentum, but she did not have time for a 1:1 sparring with everyone. On the other hand, Claude and other tools came up and suddenly there was AI-written long-form content everywhere. It just did not sound any human anymore after AI took over on it's own to prepare full content schedules. We lost even more people who were excited in the first place. As software as a service builders, we sat together and discussed how can we improve the situation for us internally and for our customers. And after watching the first Ted Lasso episode of the current season, it was obvious, what was missing: A coach that helps you become better on your own. thestory.run does exactly that. The coach asks you questions, the way a good interviewer would, until you know what you actually want to say and why it's worth someone's time. Then it hands you the arc and marks what carries the post. You write the words. Always. It never learns your style, because imitating you is just ghostwriting with extra steps. It remembers what you said you wanted to be known for, so it can tell you when you're drifting. If you want a generic post in 30 seconds, there are 50 better products here today. If you're genuinely interested in what you're posting on your profile, there's no better tool than thestory.run. To also brighten up how tools can be built in a modern age: We made it free for up to five people with no trial clock and no feature gates. Above that you pay 1 euro per coaching session and nothing else. We're super curious to see how this works. What I'd really love from you: tell me what coaches you'd love to have in your day to day live to keep getting better over time. And what kind of coaching personality would you like to have for that? We're still tuning, so let me know what you think about the product and where the coach helped you and what name you gave your coach. Mine, ofc, is called Ted. PS: Yes, once succesful, we'll drop "the" from the product name. For that, we just need our very first 18,000 coaching sessions, according to the current domain holder.

comments.text: Hello everyone. I’m Vamsi, the creator of Plane. We're excited to launch Plane Agents today.You can now add an agent to your Plane workspace the same way you'd add a team member. It gets a name, a set of projects it's allowed to work in, and work assigned to it like anyone else.What an agent is made of:• A playbook, which is the plain-language description of what it's responsible for and how it should go about it• Skills, which you build yourself and attach to an agent. Triaging incoming requests, running a standup, drafting a spec from a rough note, watching for work that's stalled. If a person can do it inside Plane, an agent can be given that job.Every action an agent takes shows up in the same activity history as your team's. And agents use the AI credits already included in paid plans, so there's no separate subscription and no per-agent seat.Very excited for everyone to try this out, we have a generous free tier to experiment with.Live on Plane Cloud now: plane.so/agents

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt,Andrian here. Some of you already use Pulsetic without knowing it: we run the public status trackers for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Vercel. On Claude alone that is 97 incidents in the last 90 days, 32 of them major, and we usually see the disruption before the official status page posts one.We first launched Pulsetic here in 2020 and have come back five times since. The gallery shows it better than I can describe it.RUM is the headline, but it isn't the only thing that shipped since we were last here:Real User MonitoringPulsetic AI, which reads your account and asks before it changes anythingAn MCP server, 17 tools, for Claude Code, Cursor and Windsurf (Team plan)Cron monitoring, on heartbeatsDomain expiry monitoringScreenshots captured at the moment a check failsAnnotations, so a deploy is marked on the response-time chartCloudflare allowlisting, which keeps our checker IPs on your firewallEngineers at large companies run this alongside their observability stack rather than instead of it, for the jobs that stack structurally cannot do: a status page that lives outside the infrastructure that is down, SLA reporting that stops being a manual month-end job, and the domains and scheduled jobs nobody owns until one of them fails quietly.If you already run traces and application-level instrumentation, we are not replacing that. Full disclosure — I'm a big fan of Anthropic and actually built an app that works exclusively with Claude Desktop for secure local file search. So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.
